title: Places, directions, and where things are
goal: Say where something is, tell apart three words that can all come out as “there is / is at” in English — 在, 有, 是 — and use place words, which always come after their noun.
bekal: use 在, 有, and 是 each in its own place
use place words: 上, 里, 旁边, 对面
give an address from big to small
ask for directions and understand the answer

dialogs.title: 对话 1 — Looking for the classroom
dialogs.intro: It's Andi's first day of teaching. He gets lost in the school building and asks a staff member. Notice three different verbs that can all be translated “is / there is”.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [请问|Qǐngwèn]，[三零五|sān líng wǔ][教室|jiàoshì][在|zài][哪儿|nǎr]？
lines.id: Excuse me, where is Room 305?
lines.literal: please — ask, three-zero-five — classroom — be-at — where.

lines.speaker: 职员:
lines.text: [在|Zài][三|sān][楼|lóu]。[上楼|Shàng lóu][以后|yǐhòu][往|wǎng][右|yòu][拐|guǎi]。
lines.id: On the third floor. Go upstairs and turn right.
lines.literal: be-at — three — floor. go-up — floor — after — toward — right — turn.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.id: Where are the stairs?
lines.literal: stairs — be-at — where.

lines.speaker: 职员:
lines.id: Next to the restroom. The elevator is across from it.
lines.literal: be-at — wash-hands-room — beside. elevator — be-at — opposite.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.id: How many classrooms are on the third floor?
lines.literal: three — floor — there-is — how-many — (measure) — classroom.

lines.speaker: 职员:
lines.text: [有|Yǒu][八|bā][个|ge]。[三零五|Sān líng wǔ][在|zài][最|zuì][里边|lǐbian]。
lines.id: Eight. Room 305 is at the very end.
lines.literal: there-is — eight — (measure). three-zero-five — be-at — most — inside.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.id: Is there a computer in the classroom?
lines.literal: classroom — inside — there-is — computer — (question).

lines.speaker: 职员:
lines.id: Yes. There's a computer on the desk.
lines.literal: there-is. desk — on — there-is — one — (measure) — computer.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.id: Great. Thank you!
lines.literal: too — good — (change). thank — you(polite).

lines.speaker: 职员:
lines.id: You're welcome. Take care!
lines.literal: not — polite. slowly — walk.

notes: **⚠️ Mandarin place words come AFTER their noun**, the reverse of English. English says “**on** the table”; Mandarin says [桌子**上**|zhuōzi shang] — “table on”. Likewise [教室**里**|jiàoshì li] “in the classroom”, [洗手间**旁边**|xǐshǒujiān pángbiān] “next to the restroom”.
**[在|zài] says where something is: A 在 place.** [教室在三楼|Jiàoshì zài sān lóu] the classroom is on the third floor. What comes before 在 is **something already known**; what comes after it is the place.

**[有|yǒu] says something exists: place 有 thing.** [桌子上有一台电脑|Zhuōzi shang yǒu yì tái diànnǎo] there's a computer on the desk. The order is the exact reverse of 在, and it introduces **something new** — like English “there is”.
**[往|wǎng] + direction + verb = “toward …”.** [往右拐|wǎng yòu guǎi] turn right, [往前走|wǎng qián zǒu] go straight ahead. This word will save you every time you ask for directions.
**[最|zuì] = most.** [最里边|zuì lǐbian] innermost, at the very end, [最好|zuì hǎo] best, [最后|zuì hòu] last.
**[台|tái] is the measure word for machines**: computers, TVs, washing machines, air conditioners. [一台电脑|yì tái diànnǎo].
**[慢走|Màn zǒu] literally “walk slowly”** is said by a host to a guest who is leaving. English has no exact match; “take care” is closest.

grammars.title: 在, 有, 是 — three words, one English translation
body: All three can come out as “is” or “there is” in English, and that's exactly why they get mixed up. What separates them is **what the speaker already knows and what is new**.

head: Word
Structure
Focus
Example
rows: The thing is known; the place is new
[书在桌子上|Shū zài zhuōzi shang]。 The book is on the table.
The place is known; the thing is new
[桌子上有书|Zhuōzi shang yǒu shū]。 There's a book on the table.
Explains what fills the whole place
[桌子上是书|Zhuōzi shang shì shū]。 What's on the table is books.

head: The question
Word used
Example
rows: [房间里有什么|Fángjiān li yǒu shénme]？
[附近有超市吗|Fùjìn yǒu chāoshì ma]？
[房间里没有人|Fángjiān li méiyǒu rén]。

after: One-second check: **if you can point at the thing, use 在; if you're introducing the thing, use 有.** “Where's the book?” → 书在哪儿. “Is there a book?” → 有书吗.
⚠️ The negative of 有 is still 没有, never 不有 — just as in Unit 2.

grammars.title: Place words — all of them come after the noun
after: ⚠️ **Place names are already places, so they don't take 里.** [我在北京|Wǒ zài Běijīng] is right; 我在北京里 is wrong. It's **objects** that need a place word: tables, bags, rooms, boxes.
With 里 and 上, the noun and the place word often fuse into one word, pronounced lightly: [家里|jiā li], [桌上|zhuō shang], [手里|shǒu li].

dialogs.title: 对话 2 — Asking for directions
dialogs.intro: Andi is looking for a bank near the school. A conversation like this is the first real test of your listening — and people's answers are usually much faster than you'd hope.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.id: Excuse me, is there a bank nearby?
lines.literal: please — ask, nearby — there-is — bank — (question).

lines.speaker: 路人:
lines.text: [有|Yǒu]。[从|Cóng][这儿|zhèr][往|wǎng][前|qián][走|zǒu]，[大概|dàgài][两|liǎng][百|bǎi][米|mǐ]。
lines.id: Yes. Go straight ahead from here, about two hundred meters.
lines.literal: there-is. from — here — toward — front — walk, roughly — two — hundred — meter.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.id: And then?
lines.literal: then — (and)?

lines.speaker: 路人:
lines.text: [到|Dào][路口|lùkǒu][往|wǎng][左|zuǒ][拐|guǎi]。[银行|Yínháng][在|zài][超市|chāoshì][对面|duìmiàn]。
lines.id: At the intersection, turn left. The bank is across from the supermarket.
lines.literal: arrive — road-mouth — toward — left — turn. bank — be-at — supermarket — opposite.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [远|Yuǎn][吗|ma]？[走路|Zǒu lù][要|yào][多长|duō cháng][时间|shíjiān]？
lines.id: Is it far? How long does it take on foot?
lines.literal: far — (question). walk — road — need — how — long — time.

lines.speaker: 路人:
lines.id: Not far, you'll be there in five minutes.
lines.literal: not — far, five — minute — just — arrive — (change).

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.id: Is there a subway station next to the bank?
lines.literal: bank — beside — there-is — underground-rail-station — (question).

lines.speaker: 路人:
lines.text: [有|Yǒu]，[二|èr][号|hào][线|xiàn]。[出口|Chūkǒu][就|jiù][在|zài][银行|yínháng][门口|ménkǒu]。
lines.id: Yes, Line 2. The exit is right outside the bank.
lines.literal: there-is, two — number — line. exit-mouth — right — be-at — bank — door-mouth.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.id: Thank you so much!
lines.literal: too — thank — you(polite) — (change).

lines.speaker: 路人:
lines.id: No need to thank me.
lines.literal: not — need — thank.

notes: **[从…往…走|cóng… wǎng… zǒu] is the frame for giving directions.** [从这儿往前走|Cóng zhèr wǎng qián zǒu] go straight ahead from here.

**[就|jiù] signals “right away, no more than that”.** [五分钟就到了|Wǔ fēnzhōng jiù dào le] you'll be there in just five minutes; [出口就在门口|Chūkǒu jiù zài ménkǒu] the exit is right there. Native speakers use this little word dozens of times a day.
**⚠️ [分|fēn] is minutes on the clock; [分钟|fēnzhōng] is a length of time.** [三点五分|sān diǎn wǔ fēn] 3:05; [五分钟|wǔ fēnzhōng] for five minutes. Mixing them up is a very common mistake.
**[多长时间|duō cháng shíjiān]？ = how long.** Literally “how long time”. A synonym is [多久|duō jiǔ].
**[口|kǒu] “mouth” is used for all kinds of openings**: [门口|ménkǒu] entrance, [路口|lùkǒu] intersection, [出口|chūkǒu] exit, [入口|rùkǒu] entrance.
**[太谢谢您了|Tài xièxie nín le]！** — the 太…了 pattern is also used to thank someone warmly, not just to complain.

grammars.title: Asking for directions and understanding the answer

head: Answers you'll hear
Meaning
rows: [往左拐|Wǎng zuǒ guǎi]。 / [往右拐|Wǎng yòu guǎi]。
It's close. / It's a bit far.

after: If the answer is too fast — and it usually is — use the two lifesavers from Unit 2: [请再说一遍|Qǐng zài shuō yí biàn] and [请说慢一点儿|Qǐng shuō màn yìdiǎnr]. Asking for a repeat is far better than walking the wrong way.

blocks.title: Restroom — the word you'll need first
items: **[洗手间|xǐshǒujiān]** — literally “hand-washing room”. The politest form, safe anywhere.
**[卫生间|wèishēngjiān]** — “hygiene room”. Just as polite, often written on signs.
**[厕所|cèsuǒ]** — direct and plain; used in public places and schools.
[洗手间在哪儿|Xǐshǒujiān zài nǎr]？ — learn it now, not later.
The door signs: [男|nán] men · [女|nǚ] women.

blocks.text: Chinese addresses are written in exactly the reverse order from English: country first, room number last. It's the same rule as for dates and names — **Mandarin always runs from big to small.**

A full example: 中国广东省广州市天河区中山路58号3楼305室 — “China, Guangdong Province, Guangzhou City, Tianhe District, No. 58 Zhongshan Road, 3rd floor, Room 305”. Read from the start, the address narrows like a funnel.

blocks.title: Useful sentences when you're lost
items: [我迷路了|Wǒ mílù le]。 — I'm lost.
[我在这儿|Wǒ zài zhèr]。 — I'm here. (pointing at the map on your phone)
[这是什么地方|Zhè shì shénme dìfang]？ — What is this place?
[您能帮我吗|Nín néng bāng wǒ ma]？ — Could you help me?
[请写下来|Qǐng xiě xiàlái]。 — Please write it down. A lifesaver: written characters are something you can show a taxi driver.
